# Raw NHANES {#project-raw-nhanes}

There is an NHANES data portal available from the **Plugins** menu, 
but it includes only a small selection of the data available.

In this project, you have to process data that's much closer to the 
original data from the government NHANES site.
It's a lot more data. 
Basically, it's more columns, and spread across many files.

It will also be more "raw," that is, it will not be decoded.
Here is the beginning of the demographics file to show you what you're up against.

```
    SEQN,SDDSRVYR,RIDSTATR,RIAGENDR,RIDAGEYR,RIDAGEMN,RIDRETH1,RIDRETH3,RIDEXMON,RIDEXAGM,DMQMILIZ,DMDBORN4,DMDYRUSR,DMDEDUC2,DMDMARTZ,RIDEXPRG,DMDHHSIZ,DMDHRGND,DMDHRAGZ,DMDHREDZ,DMDHRMAZ,DMDHSEDZ,WTINT2YR,WTMEC2YR,SDMVSTRA,SDMVPSU,INDFMPIR
    130378,12,2,1,43,NA,5,6,2,NA,2,2,6,5,1,NA,4,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,50055.450807,54374.463898,173,2,5
    130379,12,2,1,66,NA,3,3,2,NA,2,1,NA,5,1,NA,2,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,29087.450605000002,34084.721548,173,2,5
    130380,12,2,2,44,NA,2,2,1,NA,2,2,6,3,1,2,7,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,80062.674301,81196.277992,174,1,1.41
    130381,12,2,2,5,NA,5,7,1,71,NA,1,NA,NA,NA,NA,2,2,2,2,3,NA,38807.268902,55698.607106,182,2,1.53
    130382,12,2,1,2,NA,3,3,2,34,NA,1,NA,NA,NA,NA,4,2,2,3,1,2,30607.519774,36434.146346,182,2,3.6

```
This is CSV, that is, comma-separated values. 
By tradition, the attribute (column) names are in the first line.
Counting in, the fourth "column" is gender (the name of the variable is `RIAGENDR`),
followed by the age in years (`RIDAGEYR`). 
So the first person in this list is a 43-year-old male.
We'll call him "Charlie."

How do we know that "1" is Male?

For that, you need the documentation for the `RIAGENDR` attribute.
That lives on a page in a "codebook."
Here is what it looks like:

![Documentation for gender (`RIAGENDR`)](art/nhanes-riagendr-doc.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

That is, values for the sex or gender attribute 
will be `1` for `male` and `2` for `female`. 
So the third person in our file above is 44-year-old woman.

To make tables and graphs that make sense to anybody but you,
you will need to decode the values in these raw files.

::: {.datamove}
This is a job for a "calculating" or "recoding" data move,
which you can learn about in this book! 
[Here is a description](#decode-numbers-to-categories)
of how to do that for an attribute like `RIAGENDR`.
:::

### Sequence numbers 

Importantly, Charlie's "sequence number," the first item (`SEQN`), is 130378. 
You will need that!
Every person has a unique sequence number.
You will use the sequence numbers, `SEQN`, to connect data in one file to another.

For example, the "body measurements" data file starts like this:

```
    SEQN,BMDSTATS,BMXWT,BMIWT,BMXRECUM,BMIRECUM,BMXHEAD,BMIHEAD,BMXHT,BMIHT,BMXBMI,BMDBMIC,BMXLEG,BMILEG,BMXARML,BMIARML,BMXARMC,BMIARMC,BMXWAIST,BMIWAIST,BMXHIP,BMIHIP
    130378,1,86.9,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,179.5,NA,27,NA,42.8,NA,42,NA,35.7,NA,98.3,NA,102.9,NA
    130379,1,101.8,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,174.2,NA,33.5,NA,38.5,NA,38.7,NA,33.7,NA,114.7,NA,112.4,NA
    130380,1,69.4,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,152.9,NA,29.7,NA,38.5,NA,35.5,NA,36.3,NA,93.5,NA,98,NA
    130381,1,34.3,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,120.1,NA,23.8,4,NA,NA,25.4,NA,23.4,NA,70.4,NA,NA,NA
    130382,3,13.6,NA,NA,1,NA,NA,NA,1,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,1,NA,1,NA,1,NA,NA
```

See the first `SEQN`, 130378? That's Charlie!

You can see that his `BMXWT` (weight in kg) is 86.9, that is, 191 pounds.
If you count carefully over the "NA" values, you'll see that his `BMXHT` (height in cm) is 179.5, or 5 feet 10 1/2 inches. 

The upshot of this is that if you want to make one of our favorite
graphs, the one of height against age,
you will need to coordinate these two datasets.
You'll get age from the "demographics" file
and height from the "body measurements" file. 

::: {.datamove}
In CODAP, that means you'll use two tables, and connect them 
(using a "joining" data move!!)
using the sequence number `SEQN` as the connector. 

The [joining chapter](#drag-to-join-section) explains how to do that.
:::

Great! Now where do you get the data?

## Data on the NHANES site

[Here is a link to the NHANES page for data for the 2021–2023 cycle](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/continuousnhanes/default.aspx?Cycle=2021-2023){target="_blank"}.
From there you can find your way to more-current (or older) data as it becomes available. 

To get data and documentation from that page, look to the left under 
**Questionnaires, Datasets, and Related Documentation**,
then **NHANES 08/2021 to 08/2023**.
There you will see a list of categories of data: Demographics, Dietary, Examination, etc. 
If you clock on one of those, you'll see a list of data files along with links to the files themselves and to documentation. 
The rub is: the data files are in "SAS transport" format, `.xpt`. 

If you know how to cope with those, great! Go for it!

## Mostly raw data to download

For the rest of us mortals, we have converted a number of them to ordinary `csv`. 

Below, you'll see links to these, translated from `.xpt` but otherwise 
completely undecoded CSV files.
To decode them, you will need to look at the documentation for the dataset, as described above.
The "info" circles are links to the correct page on the NHANES site for the corresponding documentation file. 

#### Essential: {-}
::: {#}
<script>
    awash.insertDownloadNHANESCSV("DEMO_L", "demographics")
</script>
:::

#### Reliably interesting: {-}
::: {#}
<script>
    awash.insertDownloadNHANESCSV("BMX_L", "body measurements");
</script>
:::
